source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

17111.t:
McHenry County voted for Trump by 5 points in 2024 and for Stratton by 11 in the U.S. Senate race against Tracy, a 16-point move toward the Democrats. Stratton took 62,717 votes to Tracy's 50,147. That move ranks fifth of Illinois's 102 counties. It is larger than the state's 13-point shift and the typical Illinois county's 6, and McHenry is one of only two in the state to flip from Trump to a Democrat. Counties of similar size and 2024 vote moved less: Sangamon 6 points, Winnebago 12 and Madison 13.

Turnout was 114,667, or 71% of the 161,699 votes cast in 2024, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

17039.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, De Witt County stayed firmly Republican but moved about 7 points toward the Democrats. Tracy won 3,997 votes to Stratton's 1,760, a margin of 38 points, down from Trump's 45-point margin over Harris in 2024. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the county's shift was close to the typical Illinois county's 6 points but well short of the state's 13-point swing and the national typical move of 14.

Turnout fell to 5,850 votes, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Similar Republican counties moved alike: Bond about 7 points, Douglas 6 and Union 2.

17161.t:

Only five of Illinois' 102 counties moved further. Among similar counties, it moved more than St. Clair and Peoria but slightly less than Kane.

Turnout was 47,819 votes, 76% of the 2024 total. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell whether people changed their minds or some 2024 voters stayed home.

Turnout fell to 6,100 votes, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nearly 99% of the expected vote is counted.

In the U.S. Senate race, Warren County voted for Tracy over Stratton by 23 points, 3,507 votes to 2,176. That is 2 points toward the Democrats compared with Trump's 25-point win here in 2024, a smaller shift than in most of Illinois. The county ranks 88th of 102 by move, while the typical Illinois county moved 6 points left and the state as a whole moved 13. Similar nearby counties shifted more: Mercer by 6 points, Bureau by 5 and Fulton by 7.

Turnout was 78% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With about 90% of the expected vote counted, the numbers may still move.

17001.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Adams County stayed firmly with Republican Don Tracy, who beat Democrat Juliana Stratton 17,934 to 6,180, a margin of 48 points. That is about a point more Republican than Donald Trump's 47-point margin over Kamala Harris in 2024. The shift ran against a strong statewide current: the Democrat won Illinois by 24 points, 13 better than Harris, and 95 of the state's 102 counties moved left, typically by 6 points. Adams ranks 97th. Similar Republican counties such as Jefferson, Christian and Livingston moved 4 to 7 points toward the Democrats.

Adams cast 24,390 votes, 77% of its 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

17201.t:
In the U.S. Senate race between Stratton and Tracy, Winnebago County moved about 12 points toward the Democrats. Harris carried it by less than 1 point in 2024; Stratton won it by 13, 49,696 votes to 38,256. That shift ranks 15th among Illinois's 102 counties and beats the typical Illinois county's 6-point move, though it trails the 14-point statewide swing. Similar counties moved further: Kendall by 18, Will by 18 and DeKalb by 14.

Turnout fell sharply, with 89,375 votes cast, about 74% of the 2024 total of 121,048. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

17151.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Pope County stayed firmly Republican but moved 6 points toward the Democrats. Tracy won 1,213 votes to Stratton's 354, a margin of 54 points, compared with Trump's 60-point win here in 2024. That shift matches the typical Illinois county and sits at 51st of 102, though it is about half the statewide swing of 13 points and well below the national typical move of 14.

Only 1,588 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Nearby counties of similar size and lean split: Hardin moved 8 points left, Scott barely moved, and Brown moved 9 points right.

17087.t:
In the U.S. Senate race, Republican Tracy carried Johnson County over Democrat Stratton by 54 points, 3,534 votes to 1,029. That is a 4-point move toward the Democrats from Trump's 58-point win over Harris in 2024. Statewide, Stratton won by 24 points, a 13-point shift. The typical Illinois county moved 6 points, and Johnson ranks 70th of 102 by move. Counties with similar 2024 margins and size moved by comparable amounts: Greene 3 points, Washington 6 and White 7.

Turnout fell to 4,641 votes, 76% of the 6,103 cast in 2024. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

17035.t: Cumberland County stayed firmly Republican in the U.S. Senate race, giving Don Tracy 3,746 votes to Juliana Stratton's 927, a 60-point margin out of 4,734 ballots. That is about 2 points less Republican than Trump's 62-point win here in 2024, a smaller shift than in most of Illinois, where Stratton won statewide by 24 points and the typical county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. Cumberland ranks 86th of 102 counties by move, close to similar Pike County (2 points) but behind White and Hamilton (both about 6). Turnout was 82% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell whether the shift came from voters changing their minds or from some staying home.
